justification_text:
My point estimates reflected a broadly stable near-term outlook anchored around the prevailing price level at the time of the forecast. For the one-day horizon, the estimate of roughly 1,172–1,173 was essentially a mean-reversion anchor — assuming no major overnight catalyst, prices tend to persist close to their last observed level, so the one-day estimate was little more than the current price with a small directional lean. For the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to 1,175, reflecting a mild positive drift assumption consistent with modest risk appetite or commodity demand trends at the time. The one-month estimate of 1,182 extended that drift further, incorporating a slightly more optimistic medium-term view while acknowledging that monthly moves tend to compound small directional biases.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to historical volatility patterns at each respective horizon. Daily price ranges for the underlying asset — likely a commodity or index trading in the 1,100–1,300 range — tend to be relatively contained absent a shock, hence the relatively tight 51-point spread on the one-day interval. Over one week, uncertainty compounds meaningfully, widening to a 100-point range. By one month, the interval stretches to roughly 205 points, reflecting the well-documented reality that forecast uncertainty scales approximately with the square root of time. Liquidity conditions, macro data release schedules, and any recent volatility clustering also influenced how wide I set those bands.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside the stated intervals include sudden shifts in central bank policy signaling, particularly from the Federal Reserve or other major central banks, which can reprice commodities or risk assets sharply within hours. Geopolitical disruptions — supply chain shocks, conflict escalation, or sanctions — could create gap moves that exceed even the one-month confidence interval on either side. On the downside, an unexpected deterioration in global growth data or a sharp dollar strengthening episode could push prices well below 1,080. On the upside, a supply squeeze, inflation surprise, or flight-to-safety episode could carry prices above 1,285 within the month. These tail scenarios are real but were assigned low enough probability to sit outside the 90% interval by design.
